\c[6](I think I should leave her be…)
\c[6](I was a little apprehensive about accepting Alora’s offer and
holding the funeral service with her… Partly because I was a bit worried
about what the others would think if I spent too much time with her-)
\c[6](And partly because, even now, I really wanted to do everything I
possibly could to avoid thinking about what had happened to Akari.)
\c[6](It felt strange I’d never see her again, maybe that’s why I tried
to hide away from every reminder of it… I just wanted things to be
normal. I wanted the simplicity of my life before everything happened.)
\c[6](But life doesn’t work like that and I knew I’d have to face it
eventually.)
\c[6](So I sat quietly in the faith room, waiting for Alora to arrive.)
\c[6](...It reminded me a little bit of my meeting with Mint in here so
long ago… I suppose it was quite an easy space to reflect in. It was very
tucked away from everything else.)
\c[6](I closed my eyes and melted into the soft serenity of the cool
room, drifting into my own thoughts-)
\c[6](Only snapping back into focus when I heard a voice behind me.)
Aloranameplate
Alora2
…You came.
\c[6](She seemed oddly surprised.)
ShinkuNametag
Shinku3
Of course. I thought it could be good for both of us.
Aloranameplate
Alora2
I see…
\c[6](Alora quietly approached me and sat down next to me.)
\c[6](The two of us sat in the silence, introspecting side by side as
we looked at the altar in front of us-)
\c[6](I was not religious by any means… But perhaps I felt I needed
to repent somehow.)
\c[6](...But I had no idea what she was feeling as she stared alongside
me.)
AloraFuneralCG
lavendertheme
\c[6](Eventually, our quiet contemplation was broken by her opening her
mouth to speak-)
Aloranameplate
…You know, it’s a little funny.
…I’ve never been good with loss, even when I knew it was coming but-
With Ester, with my sister… It didn’t even really feel like I lost
anything.
I know it sounds terrible, but it always felt like an inevitability.
When my parents informed me she was gone, I didn’t even really question
what they meant.
They didn’t make a big fuss about it, so I thought if I did then I’d
be being ridiculous.
…I thought moving on and not letting those things bother you was just
part of being an adult.
…Perhaps that’s why I was so ashamed that in every other instance where
I did lose someone that I couldn’t deal with it, sensible adults were meant
to deal with it well-
So I did, at least in public. I was so ashamed of how I felt I decided
to cope in any way I could, really. Anything to keep me moving.
ShinkuNametag
…Guess it’s easier just to pretend nothing has changed at all.
It’s very easy to want to stay in the past.
…I think I never realised just how bad things had gotten between me
and Akari because I was so focused on the past, I used to practically
be her hero… I just assumed, no matter what ‘phase’ she was going
through she could never hate me.
And my parents just assumed when she was having a melt down or something
it was just her being difficult, it was always something with Akari-
So after a while I just started… Tuning it out a bit, it just became
an everyday thing.
…I guess, I just kinda thought my parents were right about her and
somewhere along the line I became complicit in it…
Aloranameplate
That’s understandable, you’re meant to listen to your parents, after all.
They are meant to guide you through life.
…Was she a bit of a trouble maker?
ShinkuNametag
…That’s an understatement.
She never really did all that well in school, it never really clicked
with her… She never found anything that she thought was worth devoting
all her time to.
If she wasn’t good at something instantly, she gave up on it pretty
instantly.
And because of that she… She got pretty involved with some bad kids
her age and that spiralled into her getting involved with the anti-ultimate
movement…
And it’s kind of hard to really parrot anything that movement was saying
when you’re actively benefiting from it-
I think she started to resent herself and all of us… And that caused
a lot of fights.
Aloranameplate
…Ester was a bit like that, always causing issues. Presumably for
attention.
I wouldn’t know, I didn’t give her much.
But even so, she had all the resources to become just like me- if she
just had the drive she’d have been able to reach a similar level of
achievement to me.
She could’ve had my life if she so wished.
But she didn’t want it… That always confused me.
Assuredly, my life was meant to be close to perfect. Many people would
do anything to be in my position.
…And yet she rejected that, in her eyes even dying was more freeing and
ideal than what would conventionally be considered good.
…Even if I can hardly recall what she was like, even when my only
clear memory of her is of a scruffy white-haired child, covered in dirt,
digging out silkworms from their enclosures and trying to bring them to
me to show me.
While thoughts of what she was like before it all happened never really
crossed my mind…
I can never stop thinking about that decision she made.
That, despite how much freedom she was given, she somehow believed
running was more liberating… That dying was more freeing.
I wonder a lot if she finally found happiness through that, or if she
regretted it.
Either way, I admit I occasionally find myself slightly jealous of
her-
ShinkuNametag
…How so?
Aloranameplate
Jealous of the fact she was able to make such a definitive decision
for herself.
That despite everything she made that decision entirely of her own
volition and had the drive to go through with it.
No matter how it turned out, I will always admire and be slightly envious
of that… My whole life I’ve simply done what I was told because it was
best.
…I thought if I saw how things ended for her I’d know for certain that
staying on the straight and narrow was indeed for the best, that I’d
have my beliefs confirmed… But-
…All I’ve really been able to glean from it, thinking back through my
decisions from the last few weeks… Is that I don’t think there really
is a solid universal best.
Different things work for different people, what might be for the
best for one person is detrimental to another.
I remember when she’d bring those silkworms to me, I was a little put
off… I thought she ought not to interfere with what they were meant
for in the lab.
But she’d argue that domesticated silkworms, when they turn into moths,
can never really fly. That they’d be stuck forever.
So she’d let them free to give them a chance to fly.
ShinkuNametag
But… If they’d lived their whole life in captivity until that point,
it’s unlikely they’d survive out in the wild long enough to turn into
moths- she knew that.
Aloranameplate
But to her, that small chance they would be able to fly… At the risk
of everything else, at the risk of certain death- was worth it. It was
better than a safe existence of being stuck.
ShinkuNametag
…You two sound quite different.
Aloranameplate
Don’t be mistaken, I’m happy with how my life ended up. I try not to
dwell on what her life was like too much.
…At the end of the day, the only thing I really do not have a satisfying
answer to is if she or I ended up happier.
ShinkuNametag
It seems like a pretty simple question to me… I mean, you got everything
you ever could have wanted.
Aloranameplate
Right, so it’s curious I cannot seem to land on an answer to it-
isn’t it?
ShinkuNametag
…I wondered a lot about that too. To me, my life was ideal.
But to Akari..? Life was unbearable.
I couldn’t understand why she was so miserable, why she didn’t just
try harder to be good, to focus on school-...
But I suppose it never crossed my mind if she was happier like that.
I just assumed she was running away from happiness because it was too
much effort.
Aloranameplate
ShinkuNametag
Either way… I’m sorry for your loss.
Aloranameplate
…I’m sorry for yours, Kutsuki.
ShinkuNametag
I don’t think I’m the one who deserves a ‘sorry’ in this situation.
…I just wish I’d said it before it was too late.
\c[6](Alora paused, doing something very strange and moving her hand
to mine… Quietly interlacing her fingers between mine and squeezing
it.)
Aloranameplate
…I think we all have things we wish we’d have said while we still had
the chance.
Aloranameplate
…Though, you really should stop being so kind to me, Kutsuki. Everyone
who attaches to me seems to die.
ShinkuNametag
Funny that… Same here.
…Maybe we’re both bad luck charms.
Aloranameplate
I suppose you’re spending so much time with me in hopes of doubling
your chances.
Well, if that’s the case. I won’t allow it. I won’t let anyone have
to mourn you.
ShinkuNametag
…That’s not it-
Aloranameplate
Then what is it?
ShinkuNametag
…I suppose, I just didn’t want you to feel alone.
Aloranameplate
…Is there really any way to stop such a feeling?
ShinkuNametag
There’s only one way to find out, isn’t there?
\c[6](The two of us sat in silence for a little longer, occasionally exchanging
a few words or thoughts…)
\c[6](But admittedly I wasn’t as open as I felt I should be… Maybe I
was still trying to run from what I’d done.)
\c[6](But on the other hand, as much as I wanted to be there for Alora,
I couldn’t let myself say too much-)
\c[6](After all, it was not just a conversation between the two of us.)
\c[6](As long as she had that earpiece in there would be others who
would be listening.)
\c[6](I just hoped she’d take it out soon and instead focus on the
people she did have left, instead of focusing on what she had lost.)
\c[6](...But maybe that was being too optimistic.)
\c[6](She was a domesticated silkmoth afterall, raised and pruned in
a glass enclosure all of her life.)
\c[6](It would take a miracle for her to be able to fly.)
\c[6](...Or maybe that’s just what we told ourselves to give us an
excuse not to try.)
\c[6](...Maybe we were just too scared of falling a few times in our
attempts.)
\c[6](Maybe we were the ones who were running.)
